purpose: Add source-exact H. A. Ironside quotations and C. H. Spurgeon illustrations for sermon preparation and presentation slides while explicitly excluding C. S. Lewis.

entries.title: Occupation with Christ
entries.author: H. A. Ironside
entries.text: The only secret of living Christ is occupation with Christ.
entries.slideText: The only secret of living Christ is occupation with Christ.
entries.sourceTitle: Holiness, the False and the True
entries.rightsBasis: The stored 1900 edition predates the 2026 U.S. public-domain cutoff; the excerpt was checked against the locally stored Internet Archive OCR.
entries.recommendedUse: Use to introduce a lesson on living with the mind and affections fixed upon Christ.
entries.reviewNote: Read the cited KJV passages in context; the quotation summarizes Ironside's application and does not replace Scripture.

entries.title: Feeding on the written Word
entries.author: H. A. Ironside
entries.text: He who feeds upon its sacred pages is feeding on Christ, for the Word written but declares the Word eternal.
entries.slideText: He who feeds upon its sacred pages is feeding on Christ
entries.sourceTitle: Holiness, the False and the True
entries.rightsBasis: The stored 1900 edition predates the 2026 U.S. public-domain cutoff; the excerpt was checked against the locally stored Internet Archive OCR.
entries.recommendedUse: Use in a study showing how Scripture bears witness to Christ.
entries.reviewNote: Use the quotation with the cited KJV passages and preserve the distinction between Christ and the written Scriptures that testify of Him.

entries.title: More than intellectual reading
entries.author: H. A. Ironside
entries.text: To read the Word in a mere intellectual manner will not minister Christ to the soul.
entries.slideText: To read the Word in a mere intellectual manner will not minister Christ to the soul.
entries.sourceTitle: Holiness, the False and the True
entries.rightsBasis: The stored 1900 edition predates the 2026 U.S. public-domain cutoff; the excerpt was checked against the locally stored Internet Archive OCR.
entries.recommendedUse: Use to distinguish information-gathering from believing, obedient reception of Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: Do not use this to disparage careful study; Ironside's point is that study must be joined to faith and spiritual response.

entries.title: Prayerful meditation
entries.author: H. A. Ironside
entries.text: But prayerful meditation on the inspired pages will nourish the soul in divine affections.
entries.slideText: But prayerful meditation on the inspired pages will nourish the soul in divine affections.
entries.sourceTitle: Holiness, the False and the True
entries.rightsBasis: The stored 1900 edition predates the 2026 U.S. public-domain cutoff; the excerpt was checked against the locally stored Internet Archive OCR.
entries.recommendedUse: Use when teaching a prayerful approach to reading and meditating upon Scripture.
entries.reviewNote: Anchor the practice in the cited KJV passages rather than treating the quotation as a formula.

entries.title: Practice before perfection
entries.author: C. H. Spurgeon
entries.text: Yet he teaches me that I must practise if I would be perfect ; must exercise myself unto godliness if I would be skilful ; must, in fact, make myself familiar with the word of God, with holy living, and saintly dying.
entries.slideText: I must practise if I would be perfect ; must exercise myself unto godliness if I would be skilful
entries.rightsBasis: The 1870 work is public domain in the United States; the excerpt was checked against the locally stored Internet Archive OCR.
entries.recommendedUse: Use the irritating flute practice as a picture of disciplined growth in Scripture and godliness.
entries.reviewNote: The illustration supports disciplined practice; salvation and sanctification must still be taught from Scripture.

entries.title: Tell the Lord so
entries.author: C. H. Spurgeon
entries.text: Mr. F. replied in a whisper, " Tell the Lord so."
entries.rightsBasis: The 1870 work is public domain in the United States; the excerpt was checked against the locally stored Internet Archive OCR.
entries.recommendedUse: Use Andrew Fuller's quiet counsel to illustrate honest dependence upon God when words fail in prayer.
entries.reviewNote: Retell the surrounding anecdote from the source when context is needed and establish prayer from the cited KJV passages.

entries.title: The bell rope of prayer
entries.author: C. H. Spurgeon
entries.text: Prayer pulls the rope below and the great bell rings above in the ears of God.
entries.slideText: Prayer pulls the rope below and the great bell rings above in the ears of God.
entries.rightsBasis: The 1870 work is public domain in the United States; the excerpt was checked against the locally stored Internet Archive OCR.
entries.recommendedUse: Use the bell-rope picture to introduce persistent prayer.
entries.reviewNote: This is a metaphor, not a mechanical promise; explain prayer according to the full teaching of the cited KJV passages.
